1 / 20 AWS Console — Logged In SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 We are logged into the AWS Workshop account in us-west-2 (Oregon). This is the hackathon environment where our IT Ticket Intelligence Agent is deployed.
2 / 20 AWS Lambda — it-ticket-agent-api SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The agent runs as a Lambda function. It receives IT ticket descriptions, runs the full AI pipeline (classify → pattern match → sub-agent → resolve), and returns structured results. No server to manage.
3 / 20 Lambda Test — CI/CD Agent (CodePipeline OOM) SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 We test the CI/CD agent directly from the Lambda console. Input: 'CodePipeline deploy failed — ECS task OOM killed'. The agent classifies it as CI/CD P2, matches a RECURRING pattern at 88% confidence, and returns the proven fix instantly — no LLM call needed for recurring issues.
4 / 20 Lambda Test — Data/ETL Agent (Glue Job Re-run) SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The Data/ETL agent handles Glue job failures. It detects the job name from the ticket description, checks the last run status (FAILED), and automatically re-triggers the job. The response includes [AUTO-ACTION] with the new Job Run ID. This is the auto-remediation feature — no human needed to restart the job.
5 / 20 CloudWatch Logs — Lambda Execution Trace SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 Every agent step emits a structured JSON log to CloudWatch. You can see: INTAKE → CLASSIFY (Bedrock Nova called) → PATTERN_MATCH → SUB_AGENT → RESOLVE. Each log entry has a timestamp, step name, status, and key data. This is the full audit trail of every ticket processed.
6 / 20 CloudWatch Logs — AgentCore Runtime Trace SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The AgentCore runtime also writes logs to CloudWatch. These show the agent initialization, memory operations, and execution lifecycle. This is separate from the Lambda logs — it shows the orchestration layer.
7 / 20 GenAI Observability Dashboard — Agent Tracing SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The GenAI Observability dashboard shows distributed traces across all agent invocations. Each trace shows the full request flow: entry → orchestration → Bedrock model call → response. This is how you monitor agent performance and identify bottlenecks in production.
8 / 20 Amazon Bedrock — Model Invocation Logs SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 Every call to Amazon Bedrock Nova Lite is logged here. You can see the model ID (us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0), input tokens, output tokens, and latency. The classifier uses ~256 tokens per call. Sub-agents use ~1024 tokens. This is where you track AI usage and costs.
9 / 20 Amazon Bedrock — Nova Lite Model Active SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 Amazon Nova Lite is the AI backbone of this solution. It replaced Claude 3 Sonnet which was marked legacy in this account. Nova Lite is fast, cost-effective, and handles both classification and fix generation. Model access is enabled at the account level here.
10 / 20 AgentCore Runtime — Agent Deployed and READY SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The agent is deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. Status: READY. This is the managed runtime that hosts our agent code. It handles scaling, memory management (STM), and provides the invocation endpoint. The agent can be invoked via CLI: agentcore invoke '{"prompt": "..."}'
11 / 20 AgentCore Runtime — Agent Detail View SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 Drilling into the agent runtime shows: deployment type (Direct Code Deploy), Python 3.12 runtime, execution role, network mode (PUBLIC), memory configuration (STM_ONLY, 30-day retention), and the S3 deployment package. The agent was last updated with the latest code including agent bus and tracing.
12 / 20 AgentCore Memory — Short-Term Memory Active SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 AgentCore Memory provides short-term memory (STM) for the agent. This allows the agent to maintain context across multiple invocations in a session. Memory ID: it_ticket_agent_agentcore_app_mem. In production, this would store ticket history and resolution patterns.
13 / 20 S3 — Domain Runbooks (Knowledge Base) SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The knowledge base lives in S3. Five domain runbooks: cicd_runbook.md, data_runbook.md, infra_runbook.md, access_runbook.md, network_runbook.md. Each sub-agent fetches its runbook before calling Bedrock, giving the AI domain-specific context. This is why the fixes are accurate and actionable, not generic.
14 / 20 S3 — Data/ETL Runbook (Glue, RDS, JDBC) SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The Data/ETL runbook is stored in S3 and fetched by the DataETLAgent before calling Bedrock. It contains step-by-step guidance for Glue job failures, JDBC timeouts, RDS connectivity issues. The AI uses this as context to generate accurate, domain-specific fix recommendations. Without the runbook, the agent still works but with lower confidence.
15 / 20 S3 — Network Runbook (VPC, ALB, Security Groups) SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The Network runbook guides the NetworkAgent on VPC troubleshooting, security group rules, ALB health checks, and API Gateway 503 errors. Each of the 5 specialist agents has its own domain runbook in S3. This is the knowledge base that makes the AI fixes actionable and accurate.
16 / 20 S3 — Static Web Dashboard Hosted SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The web dashboard is hosted as a static site on S3. No server, no EC2, no port configuration needed. The dashboard calls Lambda directly for AI processing. URL: amzn-hackthon-it-ticket-system.s3-website-us-west-2.amazonaws.com
17 / 20 Live Demo Dashboard — Ready to Accept Tickets SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The web dashboard is hosted on S3 — no server needed. It accepts IT ticket descriptions and shows the AI agent processing them in real time. Five demo scenarios are pre-loaded covering all 5 specialist agents.

20 / 20 Dashboard — Data/ETL Agent: Glue Job Auto-Remediation SLOW (3 min — full narration)
🎙 The Data/ETL agent processed the Glue job failure ticket. The flow diagram shows: Intake → Classify (Data/ETL P2) → Pattern Match (NEW) → DataETLAgent → Glue job detected → status FAILED → AUTO-RERUN triggered → RESOLVED. The fix includes [AUTO-ACTION]: Glue job re-triggered with a new Job Run ID. This is the auto-remediation feature — the agent fixed the problem without human intervention.
